summary: The note describes how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are adopting Internet of Things (IoT) technology to modernize supply chain management in late 2023. It covers uses in inventory tracking, automated procurement, fleet management, predictive maintenance and shared visibility, backed by named examples and quotes. It also notes challenges such as cost, data security and technical know-how, and stresses scalability for future growth.
one_line: IoT is helping SMEs improve supply chain tracking, procurement, delivery, maintenance and visibility, despite cost and security challenges.
key_facts: Roberta Vasquez, COO of SupplyChain Tech, said on December 12, 2023 that IoT implementations among its SME clients surged by 60% over the past fiscal year.
Large corporations were historically the primary adopters of IoT, but a growing number of SMEs were turning to it as of late November 2023.
Blooms4U, a web-based florist, began using IoT sensors on September 15, 2023 to monitor the temperature and humidity of its inventory in real-time.
Blooms4U founder Jason O'Connell reported a 20% reduction in spoilage within the first three months.
On September 30, 2023, Daniella Mwangi, procurement manager of a medium-sized electronics firm, implemented an IoT-based automated ordering system that reorders stock when levels reach a threshold.
Jake Lin, logistics director of a regional food distribution company, said on November 8, 2023 that IoT improved on-time deliveries by 35%.
Tomás García retrofitted his small manufacturing plant's machinery with IoT sensors in late September 2023 and saw unexpected machinery stoppages decrease by 50%.
Erika Schmidt, a supply chain manager at a retail company, introduced an IoT platform in early October 2023 that gives suppliers and customers access to the same real-time data.
Challenges for SMEs adopting IoT include costs that can still be prohibitive for very small enterprises, data security concerns and the technical know-how required.
Edward Kim, a cybersecurity expert for small businesses, advises working with reputable IoT solution providers who prioritize security and regularly updating software.
IoT platforms and devices must be scalable so SMEs can grow operations without complete overhauls.
Elizabeth Warren, a supply chain analyst, says SMEs can now make data-driven decisions that are timely and accurate instead of relying on estimates.
